auto: the bar shows whenever the content overflows.

Scroll down to see the rest of the note.

examples.title: Loading More at an Edge

accessibility:
- **A tab stop while it overflows:** while the content overflows on an axis it scrolls, the
  viewport has `role="region"` and `tabIndex={0}`, so a keyboard user can tab to it and scroll it
  with the arrow keys, Page Up, Page Down, Home, End and Space. Chrome and Firefox make a scroller
  reachable on their own, and Safari doesn't, which is what axe's `scrollable-region-focusable`
  rule catches. While the content fits, it's a plain box and no tab stop. One that stops
  overflowing while it has focus keeps its tab stop until focus leaves it.
- **A name:** pass `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` with a visible heading's id. It's what a
  screen reader says when the area takes focus, and a development build warns when there's
  neither.
- **The scrollbars are the system's:** ScrollArea adds no key handling and draws no bars of its
  own, so scrolling works the way it does anywhere in the browser, and the system's settings for
  its bars still apply.
- **Contrast:** the thumb is Bulma's `text-weak`, which clears WCAG's 3:1 against `scheme-main` in
  light and dark mode, and darker while the pointer is over the area.
- **Forced colors:** the bars take the system's colors on their own, the focus ring is the
  system's text color, and the fade is off.
- **More contrast:** the fade is off when the user asks for more contrast.
- **Focus ring:** Bulma's focus outline, drawn on the frame, so the fade never clips it.
- **Not live:** content that changes inside it announces nothing on its own. When loading more
  changes the content out of sight, say so in a `role="status"` region, as in
  [Loading More at an Edge](https://bestax.io/docs/api/components/scrollarea#loading-more-at-an-edge).
- **No motion:** nothing animates. Scrolling is the browser's own, so `scroll-behavior` and
  `prefers-reduced-motion` work as they do anywhere.
summary: The `ScrollArea` component renders a box whose content scrolls inside it, on the browser's own scrollbars in Bulma's colors. The bars are the system's, made thin and colored from Bulma's tokens, so they follow dark mode and keep the system's own settings. While the content overflows, the viewport is a region you can tab to and scroll by keyboard, Safari included, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. While it fits, it's a plain box. Setting the bars' colors turns off any `::-webkit-scrollbar` styles inside it.

parts.summary: The `ScrollArea` component renders a box whose content scrolls inside it, on the browser's own scrollbars in Bulma's colors. The bars are the system's, made thin and colored from Bulma's tokens, so they follow dark mode and keep the system's own settings. While the content overflows, the viewport is a region you can tab to and scroll by keyboard, Safari included, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. While it fits, it's a plain box. Setting the bars' colors turns off any `::-webkit-scrollbar` styles inside it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes for the outer frame.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the outer frame.

props.name: height
props.description: The area's height. A number is pixels, and a string is any CSS length (`"20rem"`, `"50vh"`, `"100%"`).

props.name: maxHeight
props.description: The height it grows to with its content, then scrolls past. A number is pixels. Use it in place of `height` for an area that's only as tall as it needs to be.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which way it scrolls. `vertical` and `horizontal` clip the other axis, and `both` scrolls whichever overflows.

props.name: showScrollbars
props.description: When the scrollbars show. `auto`: whenever the content overflows, the way the system shows them. `hover`: colorless until the pointer is over the area or focus is in it, which hides that the area scrolls until then, so keep it for places where the layout makes that plain. `always`: on every axis it scrolls, even when the content fits. Where the system draws its bars over the content (macOS by default, phones and tablets), they still show only while you scroll, and in forced colors they always show.

props.name: hasStableGutter
props.description: Keeps room for the vertical scrollbar whether or not it shows, so the content doesn't shift when it starts to overflow. It does nothing where the system draws its bars over the content.

props.name: hasFade
props.description: Fades the content out toward each edge that has more past it, without fading the scrollbar. It's off in forced colors and when the user asks for more contrast.

props.name: onEdgeReach
props.description: Called with the edge when scrolling reaches it, once each time it arrives, such as to load older messages at the top. It isn't called for the edge the area starts at, or when the content changes size.

extraProps.name: ref
extraProps.description: Ref forwarded to the viewport, the element that scrolls, for `scrollTo` and the like.

extraProps.name: aria-label
extraProps.description: Names the region, such as "Release notes". It needs a name, so pass this or `aria-labelledby`, and a development build warns when it has neither.

extraProps.name: aria-labelledby
extraProps.description: The id of a visible heading that names the region, in place of `aria-label`.

parts.catchAll: All standard <div> attributes and Bulma helper props
parts.helperPropsNote: The helper props go on the outer `<div>`, the `.scroll-area` frame, with `className` and `style`. The `ref`, the name, `onScroll` and the other attributes go on the `<div>` inside it, the viewport that scrolls.
